subject: Cognitive Science
title: Language Attrition
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Language Attrition.

hook.text: An immigrant returns home after 20 years and finds her first language feels clumsy. She pauses, searches for words she once knew.

buildup.text: Language attrition is the gradual loss of a language you stop using. It begins with vocabulary and expression.

discovery.text: The first language doesn't vanish, though. Brain studies show it's still represented—just harder to access.

twist.text: Relearning a 'lost' language is dramatically faster than learning a new one. The pathways are dormant, not destroyed.

climax.text: If you learned the language before age 12, the core grammar typically survives attrition even decades later.

punchline.text: A neglected language fades but rarely dies.

quiz.question: What happens to a first language that stops being used?
options: It becomes harder to access but persists
